name: aave-usdc-protective-exit
description: Protective exit for a Safe's Aave v3 Base USDC supply position: watch the supply APR, run Exit Keepa's deterministic policy gate, simulate execTransactionWithRole through the Safe's Zodiac Roles Modifier, and stop there. The broadcast step is described but disabled.

broadcast.note: Nothing in this repository registers or runs this document, and no code path here sends simulate: false on its behalf. The broadcast step is written down so the shape of the authorized write is reviewable, not so it can be triggered from this file.

steps.description: Read the live Aave v3 Base USDC supply APR and compare it against the strategy's threshold. Nothing downstream runs unless this crosses.

Exit Keepa's own deterministic gate (apps/api/src/agent/policy.ts). Plain boolean and string comparisons - no model, no heuristic. Every check must pass or the attempt is refused before KeeperHub is contacted at all.
Dry run against real chain state: execTransactionWithRole on the Safe's Roles Modifier, simulate: true. A revert here is a hard stop - the exit ends failed and nothing is sent.

innerCall.signature: withdraw(address asset, uint256 amount, address to)

steps.description: The real write: the byte-identical body from the simulate step with simulate removed and an Idempotency-Key attached. Disabled here. In the running product this step is apps/api/src/execution/executeApproved.ts over Direct Execution REST, which is what produced the live proof.

innerCall.signature: withdraw(address asset, uint256 amount, address to)

notes: This is the agent-authored workflow surface. It describes the exit as a KeeperHub workflow so the authorized write is inspectable before anything runs.

Exit Keepa's live proof did NOT go through this surface. It went through KeeperHub's Direct Execution REST API - POST /execute/contract-call with simulate: true, then the same body with an Idempotency-Key, then GET /execute/{executionId}/status until a receipt confirmed it. See docs/SUBMISSION.md section 6.

recipient is the literal string "safe": the Roles Modifier's own parameter condition already fixes `to` to the Safe, and Exit Keepa's policy check fixes it again independently. Neither this document nor any caller can name a different recipient.
The withdraw amount is Aave's max-uint256 sentinel, which self-limits to whatever the position actually holds.
